items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: I used to go to work every night in “Black and Blue,” oh is Sir Roland Hanna going to play tonight.

ctx.x: Did you have something you did when you were in the pit to help keep focused when you had 84 measures of rest and then you had to come in? Because it’s been my observation that, you know when you play a show over and over and over you have these long periods of not playing that your mind can start going out.

You know what? That’s a brilliant point. And my experience is totally — because that’s the norm. See that’s the norm. It’s going to the assembly line. You have to realize I had a very, very unique Broadway career. In other words I went to “Sophisticated Ladies” to a show called “Black and Blue” you know which was filled with jazz all-stars. I did “Jelly’s Last Jam” where the clarinet was just all throughout the whole thing. And most of my shows have not been your typical Broadway shows, you see they’ve been jazz-…
It’s okay with me if you brag.
